findings.title: UnixFileLock follows symlinks when opening the lock file with O_TRUNC, allowing arbitrary file truncation
findings.evidence: UnixFileLock._acquire() builds open_flags = os.O_RDWR | os.O_TRUNC (line 41) and then calls os.open(self.lock_file, open_flags, self._context.mode) (line 44). The call passes no os.O_NOFOLLOW, so the kernel resolves any symbolic link at the lock path and applies O_TRUNC to the link target. Because os.open() runs with the victim process's privileges, the attacker never needs write permission on the target file. Reachability: an attacker with local filesystem access who can control or predict the lock path (the common case for lock files placed in shared/predictable directories such as /tmp or a per-user cache dir) pre-creates a symlink pointing at the victim file; when the application acquires the lock, the target is truncated to zero bytes. The exploit is deterministic in the pre-existing-symlink case, and even when the path is instead checked first, line 42 `if not Path(self.lock_file).exists()` is a non-atomic stat (CWE-367 TOCTOU) whose result can be invalidated before line 44, so an attacker can swap in a symlink in the gap (the advisory confirms exploitation in 1-3 attempts). The same sink is inherited by AsyncUnixFileLock in filelock/asyncio.py, which just schedules _acquire via _run_internal_method. This is CVE-2025-68146 / GHSA-w853-jp5j-5j7f, fixed upstream in 3.20.1 by adding O_NOFOLLOW to this os.open() call; the target still has the vulnerable pre-3.20.1 code.

findings.title: WindowsFileLock follows reparse points (symlinks/junctions) when opening the lock file with O_CREAT|O_TRUNC
findings.evidence: WindowsFileLock._acquire() calls raise_on_not_writable_file(self.lock_file) (line 20, a stat-based, non-atomic check) and ensure_directory_exists() (line 21), then builds flags = os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC (lines 22-26) and calls os.open(self.lock_file, flags, self._context.mode) (line 28). The code never inspects FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT / calls GetFileAttributesW, so os.open follows an existing symlink or directory junction at the lock path and O_TRUNC zeroes the link target. Reachability: a local attacker able to create symlinks (Windows 10+ Developer Mode, or any user with SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege) who controls or predicts the lock path places a symlink/junction at that path; when the victim process acquires the lock, the pointed-to file is truncated using the victim's privileges. The stat performed by raise_on_not_writable_file follows the link and therefore does not block the attack, and the gap between that check and os.open is a CWE-367 TOCTOU window. The same sink is inherited by AsyncWindowsFileLock in filelock/asyncio.py. Fixed upstream in filelock 3.20.1 by adding a GetFileAttributesW reparse-point check before opening; the target retains the vulnerable pre-3.20.1 code (CVE-2025-68146 / GHSA-w853-jp5j-5j7f).
